title: termal_followup_session bypasses the four-active-delegation cap when re-arming a terminal child
outcome:
Found by the Codex reviewer 2026-07-16 (Medium). Distinct from the tm-ds1 re-arm race and from tm-px5's stale-result-packet bug.

Delegation creation enforces a four-active-delegation cap per parent via active_delegation_count_for_parent (src/delegations.rs:483 and :538). followup_delegation re-arms a TERMINAL child back to Running (src/delegations.rs:1073, rearm_terminal_delegation_for_followup_locked) WITHOUT consulting that cap.

Effect: a parent already at four active delegations can resume any number of previously-completed children via termal_followup_session, so the concurrency limit the creation path enforces is unbounded in practice. Each resumed child spawns/attaches a real agent runtime, so this is a resource limit, not a cosmetic one.

Fix: enforce the same cap inside the re-arm, under the same lock that performs the Completed/Failed -> Running gate (so the check and the transition stay atomic — see tm-ds1 for why that lock boundary matters). Return the same 409-shaped ApiError the creation path uses when at capacity.

Test: a parent at the cap must have termal_followup_session on a completed child rejected; below the cap it must succeed. Neuter-verify (remove the check, watch the test fail).
